{{nihongo|'''Yokota Shrine'''|横田神社 (総社市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Bitchū Province]].

It is one of the seven shrines in Sōja counted as Engishiki-listed shrines, being a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}} (small) of {{ill|Katō district|ja|下道郡|zh|下道郡|qid=Q10868734}}, {{ill|Bitchū Province|cs|Provincie Biččú|de|Provinz Bitchū|es|Provincia de Bitchū|fa|ولایت بیچو|fi|Bitchūn provinssi|fr|Province de Bitchū|gl|Provincia de Bitchū|id|Provinsi Bitchū|it|Bitchū|ja|備中国|ko|빗추국|lt|Bičiū žemė|nl|Bitchu (provincie)|pt|Província de Bitchū|ru|Биттю (провинция)|simple|Bitchū Province|sk|Biččú|sr|Провинција Бичу|tr|Bitchū (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Біттю|zh|備中國|zh_min_nan|Bittyû-kok|qid=Q1047514}}. It stands in the Kushiro area in western Sōja, on the southern foot of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Masakiyama}}, and its {{ill|Ujiko|Q125562175|qid=Q125562175}} area covers central and northwestern parts of that district (koaza names: Bessho, Yokota, Origami, Yamaguchi, Shimizu, Oshikida). Former rank was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
It enshrines {{ill|Ame no Hohi|bg|Аме Но Хохи|fa|آمه-نو-هوهی|fr|Ame no Hohi|it|Ame no Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ|pl|Niebiański Duch Przewodni|ru|Амэ но Хохи|simple|Ame no Hohi|zh|天菩比神|qid=Q10940685|lt=Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}, with divine virtues such as academic success and wish fulfillment.

=== Origin ===
Founding era is unknown. One tradition says that when {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}} stayed at a temporary palace here, {{ill|Emperor Kōbun|Q357242|qid=Q357242|lt=Prince Ōtomo}} (son of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|Q314802|qid=Q314802}}) attacked with a great army to overthrow him. The emperor purified himself, worshiped heaven and earth deities, prayed for victory, defeated Prince Ōtomo's army, then built and revered a small shrine, which became Yokota Shrine<ref>'{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku}}' quoting 'Kibi District Shrine Record.'</ref>.

According to a precinct {{ill|Stele|Q178743|qid=Q178743}} (built {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 3 / {{ill|1836|Q7601|qid=Q7601}}) and other materials, the shrine declined once in the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, then was revived in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 13 ({{ill|1585|Q6736|qid=Q6736}}) as '''Tenjingū'''.

Later it was redeveloped between around {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 10 ({{ill|1827|Q7008|qid=Q7008}}) and Tenpō 7 (1836), and renamed again as '''Yokota Shrine'''. The current buildings are from around that period.

Formerly, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shōrinzan Shōfuku-ji}} in Bessho, west of the shrine site, served as the shrine's {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}}.

=== Festivals ===
*{{ill|April 29|Q2535|qid=Q2535}} - Spring Festival
*{{ill|August 4|Q2784|qid=Q2784}} - Summer Festival
*{{ill|October 21|Q2960|qid=Q2960}} and {{ill|October 22|Q2957|qid=Q2957|lt=22}} - Autumn Festival (with dedication of Bitchū Kagura)
Three festivals are held yearly (spring, summer, autumn); the autumn one is especially large, and {{ill|Bichu Kagura|Q11387313|qid=Q11387313}} is dedicated in the {{ill|Kagura-den|Q94498|qid=Q94498}} described below.

=== Shrine buildings ===
Current shrine buildings were completed around {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 10. The honden is 1-ken wide and 2-ken deep, {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}}, hira-iri. A southern {{ill|corridor|Q106426877|qid=Q106426877}} links it to the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}}. Corridors extend east, west, and south from the haiden; especially the south corridor is long, and from above the complex appears in a distinct cross-like plan. West of the haiden is the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shamusho}}, east is Tenjingū enshrining Sugawara no Michizane, and at the end of the southern corridor stands a zuijin gate.

=== Precinct ===
Unusually for a shrine, it has a {{ill|Shōrō|Q1363585|qid=Q1363585}}. A kaguraden is also built on the south side of the precinct. Many small precinct shrines are enshrined within the grounds.

=== Access ===
From {{ill|Sōja Station|Q844657|qid=Q844657}} on JR {{ill|Hakubi Line|Q844666|qid=Q844666}}, JR {{ill|Kibi Line|Q844682|qid=Q844682}}, or {{ill|Ibara Railway|Q11373397|qid=Q11373397}}, take a {{ill|Chutetsu Bus|Q11367772|qid=Q11367772}} bound for {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Niimoto}}; get off at Yokota stop and walk about 3 minutes.
